title: Week 2 Of The AI Gaming Festival | Graphics, Planning and Raising Capital
author: bingewavecinema
selftext:
We're entering Week 2 of the AI Gaming Festival! It's been really fun and a great learning experience for the developers and games participating.

Here's a recap of last week and what's happening this week.

# Recap

*(Recordings and materials are available for download.)*

1. [Core Loops](https://www.glitch.fun/gameshows/9eadde86-a1b2-4882-86e4-a3e9e2e08814/schedule/019fa978-7e82-72c7-b9f2-a1b7e5287d08/standalone): This is a must-attend session whether you use AI or not. It covers core loops, sub-loops, pacing, progression, and rewards, and how to make your game do what it's supposed to do: provide a fun and rewarding experience.
2. [Intro to Vibe Coding Games](https://www.glitch.fun/gameshows/9eadde86-a1b2-4882-86e4-a3e9e2e08814/schedule/01a03fcd-b688-71c7-ad3a-0418370edb3b/standalone): An introduction to vibe coding games. It covers different prompt types, setting up Claude and Codex, and the homework for creating your first game.

The homework was given because we want developers and vibe coders to apply what they learn from the talks.

# This Week: Graphics, Planning, and Raising Capital

1. [Gemini and AI Game Development](https://www.glitch.fun/gameshows/9eadde86-a1b2-4882-86e4-a3e9e2e08814/schedule/01a046a3-2784-7194-b53c-a02148c1397e/standalone): Learn how Gemini can be used for AI game development, including some of its most unique use cases.
2. [Intro to Building Graphics](https://www.glitch.fun/gameshows/9eadde86-a1b2-4882-86e4-a3e9e2e08814/schedule/01a0542f-17f4-726d-a334-91ddc8d4bf4c/standalone): This session will teach you how to create graphics for your game with AI from scratch, the steps to get them to a really high quality, and when to hire someone to polish your game.
3. [Raising $11 Million for Your Game](https://www.glitch.fun/gameshows/9eadde86-a1b2-4882-86e4-a3e9e2e08814/schedule/019fd2ce-a356-7301-8493-16ba09bf8093/standalone): Told from the perspective of a game developer who raised $11 million from top VCs for their studio, and what they are doing now.
4. [Raising Capital for Your Game](https://www.glitch.fun/gameshows/9eadde86-d966-7094-ace3-fdfded808ed1/standalone): Told from the perspective of a VC, covering what they look for when funding your game.
5. [Planning Before Prompting](https://www.glitch.fun/gameshows/9eadde86-a1b2-4882-86e4-a3e9e2e08814/schedule/019f8136-d966-7094-ace3-fdfded808ed1/standalone): What to do before you even begin coding your game with AI and how to prepare.

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body:
For the people who are complaining about charging, and this is Reddit so I expect to get downvoted, but I want you to think about how much work goes into setting an event that benefits others:

1. There months of networking, messaging people on LinkedIn to convince them to come out and share their knowledge about game development.
2. Then there is lots of time spent rehearsing with each speaker, make sure they are setup
3. Then there is a lot of time putting actually putting together the lessons for the events. A single powerpoint/lesson plan takes about 3-5 hours, even with AI. Now let's do 20 of them.
4. There is months that goes into marketing the event and promoting to create awareness of people to come
5. There is time spent building out the platform
6. There are costs incurred for the technology used for streaming the event; live streaming and video conferencing is not free. Server hosting isn't free either when you have to setup custom severs.
7. There is costs that goes into advertising the event.
8. Then there is the time spent manage 2 platforms, Glitch and Steam, with games constantly to go up, taken down, re-ordered, etc.
9. Receive daily hate email and constant basis for putting together the event.

Who else wants to do all of the above for free? Who is actively doing this?

So to say "its bad form to charge for this", its worse form for someone to expect someone else to spend lots of their time and money to put together an event that helps multiple people out and pushes the community forward, and get nothing in return.

replies.author: bingewavecinema
replies.body:
Personally, thats how I've always taught (I use to teach coding bootcamps years before AI as a part time night job), and I think that is where the best users of AI will be, those that critically think.

Example: Using OpenAI image generation, you might be making a game with children in (exploitative way), ie Alice in Wonderland game.

You tell OpenAI to make a picture of Alice looking scared, it tells you no that's its against its child safety regulation.

So how do you solve this?

Create a new prompt to say "Create an image with Alice with her yes really wide, pupils dilated, mouth in circle, eye brows raised".

OpenAI creates the image based on the description.
